═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

PATTERN:
  New code deployed with @Value("${some.property}") 
  → property missing from ConfigMap

Fix process:
  kubectl logs <crashing-pod> -c <container> --previous | grep "Could not resolve"
  → Add missing property to ConfigMap
  → kubectl rollout restart deployment/<name> -n itariff-api

{
  "AllowedHeaders": ["*"],
  "AllowedMethods": ["GET", "HEAD"],
  "AllowedOrigins": ["https://intranet-dev.allcargoapps.com", "https://intranet-uat.allcargoapps.com", "https://intranet.allcargoapps.com", "https://intellihub.allcargoapps.com"],
  "MaxAgeSeconds": 3600
}

1. Find account owning allcargo-intranet bucket and apply CORS

chunks.heading: Project: Tag-Based Pod Resource Billing Monitor
chunks.content:
# Project: Tag-Based Pod Resource Billing Monitor
**Created**: 2026-06-11  
**Scope**: itariff, prefiler, itopaz — SIT EU, DEV EU clusters  
**Goal**: Allocate Kubernetes pod resource costs (CPU/memory) per product using a single `app` label tag (`itariff` / `itopaz` / `prefiler`), and surface billing breakdowns via AWS Cost Explorer + Kubecost/CloudWatch

---

chunks.heading: Project: Tag-Based Pod Resource Billing Monitor > 1. Tagging Strategy > 1.1 Tag Label (per pod)
chunks.content:
### 1.1 Tag Label (per pod)
One label added to all pods — **`billing-app`**:

| Label Key | Values | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `billing-app` | `itariff` / `prefiler` / `itopaz` | Product-level billing grouping |

Every pod in an itariff namespace gets `billing-app: itariff`, prefiler pods get `billing-app: prefiler`, itopaz pods get `billing-app: itopaz`.

> **Why `billing-app` and not `app`**: Pods already have `app: <service-name>` used by selectors/services. Overwriting it would break routing. Using `billing-app` keeps billing separate without touching existing selectors.

chunks.heading: Project: Tag-Based Pod Resource Billing Monitor > 1. Tagging Strategy > 1.2 AWS Node Tags (EKS Node Groups)
chunks.content:
### 1.2 AWS Node Tags (EKS Node Groups)
| AWS Tag Key | Value |
|---|---|
| `Project` | `itopaz` |
| `Environment` | `sit` / `dev` |
| `BillingApp` | `itariff` / `prefiler` / `itopaz` (per node group if split) |
| `CostCenter` | `allcargo-ecu` |

chunks.heading: Project: Tag-Based Pod Resource Billing Monitor > 3. Implementation Steps > Phase 1 — Add Label to Deployment YMLs in Repos
chunks.content:
### Phase 1 — Add Label to Deployment YMLs in Repos

Under `spec.template.metadata.labels`, add one line:
```yaml
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: <existing-service-name>   # keep as-is
        billing-app: itariff           # add this (itariff / prefiler / itopaz)
```

**Repos to update:**
- `itariff-k8s-repo` → `uat` branch → `billing-app: itariff`
- `prefiler-k8s-repo` → `sit` branch → `billing-app: prefiler`
- `itopaz-k8s-repo` → SIT branch → `billing-app: itopaz`
- Repeat for DEV branches

chunks.heading: Project: Tag-Based Pod Resource Billing Monitor > 3. Implementation Steps > Phase 2 — Patch Live Clusters (no redeploy needed)
chunks.content:
### Phase 2 — Patch Live Clusters (no redeploy needed)

**SIT EU — itariff namespaces:**
```bash
for ns in itariff-api itariff-bff itariff-ui; do
  kubectl get deploy -n $ns --no-headers -o name | xargs -I{} \
    kubectl patch {} -n $ns --type=merge \
    -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"labels":{"billing-app":"itariff"}}}}}'
done
```

**SIT EU — prefiler namespaces:**
```bash
for ns in prefiler-api prefiler-bff prefiler-ui; do
  kubectl get deploy -n $ns --no-headers -o name | xargs -I{} \
    kubectl patch {} -n $ns --type=merge \
    -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"labels":{"billing-app":"prefiler"}}}}}'
done
```

**SIT EU — itopaz namespaces:**
```bash
for ns in itopaz-auth itopaz-export itopaz-platform; do
  kubectl get deploy -n $ns --no-headers -o name | xargs -I{} \
    kubectl patch {} -n $ns --type=merge \
    -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"labels":{"billing-app":"itopaz"}}}}}'
done
```

> Repeat for DEV EU — same commands via `dev/eu/dev-eu-bastion.pem` to `10.100.145.118`

chunks.heading: Prefiler Service Configuration > Architecture Note: single-spa Child Microfrontends Cannot Render Standalone
chunks.content:
## Architecture Note: single-spa Child Microfrontends Cannot Render Standalone
- `prefiler-ui` namespace apps (`imdg-prefiler`, `afr-prefiler`, etc.) are single-spa **children**, built via `main.single-spa.ts` — they export `bootstrap`/`mount`/`unmount` lifecycle hooks and do not self-render on script load
- The shell (`microfrontend-main`) boots `single-spa` + `single-spa-layout` at root `/` and mounts the correct child based on the current browser URL
- The `prefiler-ui` VirtualService routes `/<app>-prefiler/*` by path prefix **directly to each child's pod**, bypassing the shell — a full-page navigation/refresh/deep-link to that path never loads the shell, so the child's `main.js` loads but is never `mount()`ed → blank page
- Each child's `.htaccess` has (or needs) a guard that hands off full-page navigation to the shell instead of trying to render standalone or hardcoding a 301 to a fixed path (which drops the destination) — see `changes-log.md` 2026-07-24 entry for the `imdg-prefiler` fix pattern (redirect to shell `/dashboard?spaRedirect=<encoded original path>`, shell restores URL via `history.replaceState` before single-spa boots)
- This pattern has not been checked/fixed yet in the other 11 `*-prefiler` UI repos

chunks.heading: Singapore Cluster - Istio IngressGateway Critical Fix
chunks.content:
# Singapore Cluster - Istio IngressGateway Critical Fix
*Date: June 5, 2026*

chunks.heading: Singapore Cluster - Istio IngressGateway Critical Fix > Incident Summary
chunks.content:
## Incident Summary
- **Severity**: CRITICAL
- **Cluster**: apse1-itopaz-sit-eks (ap-southeast-1)
- **Impact**: Complete ingress routing failure, cluster overloaded with 12,599 pods

chunks.heading: Singapore Cluster - Istio IngressGateway Critical Fix > Root Cause
chunks.content:
## Root Cause
1. Operator (jump server history line 937) ran: `k delete gw itopaz-gateway -n istio-system`
2. Gateway recreation triggered HPA to scale `istio-ingressgateway` deployment
3. New pods scheduled on Windows node (`ip-10-130-211-18`) which **does not support Linux sysctl syscalls** required by Envoy proxy
4. Every pod failed with `SysctlForbidden` status immediately
5. HPA continuously retried → cascading creation of 12,500+ stuck pods
6. All pods stuck as `0/1 SysctlForbidden` — ingress completely broken

chunks.heading: Singapore Cluster - Istio IngressGateway Critical Fix > Symptoms
chunks.content:
## Symptoms
```
kubectl get pods -n istio-system | grep SysctlForbidden | wc -l
# Output: 12501
kubectl get pods --all-namespaces | wc -l
# Output: 12599
```

chunks.heading: Singapore Cluster - Istio IngressGateway Critical Fix > Fix Applied (June 5, 2026) > Step 1: Add Linux-only node affinity to deployment
Singapore Cluster - Istio IngressGateway Critical Fix > Fix Applied (June 5, 2026) > Step 2: Delete old stuck ReplicaSets with cascade
chunks.content:
### Step 2: Delete old stuck ReplicaSets with cascade
```bash
kubectl delete rs istio-ingressgateway-6bcb465c5f istio-ingressgateway-696f57d5 \
  -n istio-system --cascade=foreground
```

chunks.heading: Singapore Cluster - Istio IngressGateway Critical Fix > Fix Applied (June 5, 2026) > Step 3: Force delete remaining stuck pods
chunks.content:
### Step 3: Force delete remaining stuck pods
```bash
kubectl delete pods -n istio-system -l app=istio-ingressgateway --grace-period=0 --force
```

chunks.heading: Singapore Cluster - Istio IngressGateway Critical Fix > Result
chunks.content:
## Result
| Metric | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| Total cluster pods | 12,599 | 97 |
| istio-system pods | 12,507 | 7 |
| ingressgateway pods | 12,501 failed | 1 running |
| All nodes | Overloaded | Ready |

chunks.heading: Singapore Cluster - Istio IngressGateway Critical Fix > HPA Configuration
chunks.content:
## HPA Configuration
```
NAME                   MIN   MAX   REPLICAS
istio-ingressgateway   1     5     1
```

chunks.heading: Singapore Cluster - Istio IngressGateway Critical Fix > Prevention
chunks.content:
## Prevention
The `istio-ingressgateway` deployment now has permanent `nodeAffinity` for `kubernetes.io/os: linux`.
This prevents scheduling on Windows nodes in future.

chunks.heading: iTariff Project — Knowledge Transfer (KT) Document > 11. CI/CD — Jenkins Pipelines > UAT → PROD Promotion Pipeline
chunks.content:
### UAT → PROD Promotion Pipeline
Located at: `itariff-k8s-repo` (promote Jenkinsfile)

**Key parameters:**
| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `SERVICE_NAME` | Service to promote (free-text, e.g. `tariff-geo-service`) |
| `IMAGE_TAG_OVERRIDE` | Optional: specific SIT image tag or full URI |
| `DEPLOYMENT_FILE` | K8s manifest filename (defaults to SERVICE_NAME) |
| `SKIP_TRIVY_SCAN` | Skip security scan (not recommended) |
| `SKIP_DEPLOYMENT` | Promote image only, skip EKS deploy |

**Promotion stages:**
1. Validate Parameters
2. Send Start Notification (Teams)
3. Resolve UAT image tag from SIT ECR
4. Pull UAT image from SIT ECR (`464134132424`)
5. Re-tag: `*-sit-<sha>` → `*-prod-<sha>`
6. Trivy security scan (blocks push on CRITICAL CVEs)
7. Push to PROD ECR (`965031587107`)
8. Checkout K8s manifests (`itariff-k8s-repo`, branch: `prod`)
9. Update image tag in manifest + git push
10. `kubectl apply` → PROD EKS (`euc1-itopaz-prd-eks`)

chunks.heading: iTariff Project — Knowledge Transfer (KT) Document > 15. Known Issues & Operational Notes > DB Performance Issue — `/selling-rates/import` 8–10s Load Time
chunks.content:
### DB Performance Issue — `/selling-rates/import` 8–10s Load Time

**Environment**: SIT EU (`itariff-euat.itopazapp.com/selling-rates/import`)  
**Root cause**: `dbo.tariff` (146 GB) and `dbo.tariffdetails` (184 GB) have **no indexes** on lookup columns → full sequential scans on every BFF dropdown call (~10 parallel on page load).

**Slow endpoints confirmed:**
| Endpoint | Latency | Cause |
|----------|---------|-------|
| `GET /bffdropdown/getTSOCPOL` | 1,946ms | Full seq scan on `dbo.tariff` |
| `GET /bffdropdown/getPOR` | 1,588ms | Full seq scan on `dbo.tariff` |
| `POST REDACTED_SECRET_KEY_PLACEHOLDER_40_CHARSSingleRow1` | 343–1,798ms | `gettariffmainsearchsinglerow_db` stored proc, full scan |
| `POST REDACTED_SECRET_KEY_PLACEHOLDER_40_CHARSngleRow` | 1,774ms | Full scan |

**Fix required (dev team):**
```sql
-- Run on TariffSelling DB (itariff-sit-cluster)
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_tariff_pol ON dbo.tariff(pol_code);
```

chunks.heading: iTariff Project — Knowledge Transfer (KT) Document > 17. Backup & Recovery > 17.1 Aurora PostgreSQL (RDS)
chunks.content:
### 17.1 Aurora PostgreSQL (RDS)

| Resource | Cluster | Retention | Backup Window (UTC) | Engine |
|----------|---------|-----------|-------------------|--------|
| DEV EDI DB | `euc1-itariff-edi-dev` | **7 days** | 20:26–20:56 | Aurora PostgreSQL 15.15 |
| DEV App DB | `euc1-itopaz-dev-database-cluster` | **7 days** | 08:42–10:42 | Aurora PostgreSQL 16.11 |
| SIT Tariff DB | `itariff-sit-cluster` | **7 days**  | — | Aurora PostgreSQL |

- Backups are **automated by AWS RDS** — snapshots taken daily, kept for 7 days.
- Snapshot naming pattern: `rds:<cluster-id>-YYYY-MM-DD-HH-MM`
- Confirmed snapshots (DEV EDI): Jul 4, Jul 6, Jul 8 — all `available`.

**Restore a snapshot (CLI):**
```bash
# List automated snapshots
aws rds describe-db-cluster-snapshots --region eu-central-1 \
  --db-cluster-identifier euc1-itariff-edi-dev \
  --snapshot-type automated \
  --query "DBClusterSnapshots[*].{ID:DBClusterSnapshotIdentifier,Created:SnapshotCreateTime,Status:Status}" \
  --output table

# Restore to new cluster from snapshot
aws rds restore-db-cluster-from-snapshot \
  --region eu-central-1 \
  --db-cluster-identifier euc1-itariff-edi-dev-restored \
  --snapshot-identifier rds:euc1-itariff-edi-dev-2026-07-08-04-37 \
  --engine aurora-postgresql \
  --engine-version 15.15
```

chunks.heading: Other Booking Service - Request Timeout Analysis (Dev)
chunks.content:
# Other Booking Service - Request Timeout Analysis (Dev)

**Date:** 19-May-2026  
**Service:** tariff-buying-otherbooking-service  
**Namespace:** itariff-api  
**Cluster:** euc1-itopaz-dev-eks  

---

chunks.heading: Other Booking Service - Request Timeout Analysis (Dev) > What Happened
chunks.content:
## What Happened

After applying `JAVA_OPTS` env var to fix potential OOM, the deployment triggered a rolling restart. During the restart, upstream services (e.g., `tariff-selling-bff`) received **request timeout** errors when calling the Other Booking service.

---

chunks.heading: Other Booking Service - Request Timeout Analysis (Dev) > Root Cause > 1. Slow Application Startup (~91 seconds)
chunks.content:
### 1. Slow Application Startup (~91 seconds)
- The Spring Boot app takes **91.4 seconds** to fully initialize
- Kafka listeners, DB connections, and Spring context all load during this time
- The DispatcherServlet only initializes on the **first HTTP request** (lazy init)

chunks.heading: Other Booking Service - Request Timeout Analysis (Dev) > Root Cause > 2. Rolling Deployment Gap
chunks.content:
### 2. Rolling Deployment Gap
- Kubernetes rolling update terminates old pods before new pods are fully warm
- The readiness probe may pass (port open) before the app is truly ready to handle requests
- During the ~90s startup window, requests routed to new pods fail with timeout

chunks.heading: Other Booking Service - Request Timeout Analysis (Dev) > Root Cause > 3. Istio Sidecar Interaction
chunks.content:
### 3. Istio Sidecar Interaction
- Istio proxy (envoy) starts before the app container is ready
- Upstream services see the pod as "ready" via Istio, but the app isn't serving yet
- Default Istio timeout (15s) is shorter than app startup time, causing caller-side timeouts

---

chunks.heading: Other Booking Service - Request Timeout Analysis (Dev) > Evidence from Logs
chunks.content:
## Evidence from Logs

```
Started TariffBuyingOtherbookingSvcApplication in 91.396 seconds (process running for 96.751)
```

First HTTP request received at **05:30:38** (after full startup):
```
Initializing Spring DispatcherServlet 'dispatcherServlet'
Request [/tariff-selling-bff] received http: {url: /buying-otherbooking-domain-REDACTED_SECRET_KEY_PLACEHOLDER_40_CHARStherSearchSingleRow, method: POST}
```

---

chunks.content:
## Pod Configuration

| Setting | Value |
|---------|-------|
| Replicas | 2 |
| Memory Limit | 1Gi |
| Memory Request | 800Mi |
| CPU Limit | 500m |
| CPU Request | 100m |
| Image | tariff-buying-otherbooking-service-dev-4d7a59da |

---

chunks.heading: Other Booking Service - Request Timeout Analysis (Dev) > Why JAVA_OPTS Didn't Work
chunks.content:
## Why JAVA_OPTS Didn't Work

The `JAVA_OPTS` environment variable was set but **not picked up** by the application. This is because:
- The app's Dockerfile/entrypoint does not reference `$JAVA_OPTS`
- Only `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS` is auto-read by the JVM without app changes

---

chunks.heading: Other Booking Service - Request Timeout Analysis (Dev) > Recommendations > Immediate Fix (Prevent Timeout During Restarts)
chunks.content:
### Immediate Fix (Prevent Timeout During Restarts)
1. **Increase readiness probe `initialDelaySeconds`** to 100s so pods aren't marked ready before app starts
2. **Use `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS`** instead of `JAVA_OPTS` for JVM flags to be auto-picked

chunks.heading: Other Booking Service - Request Timeout Analysis (Dev) > Recommendations > Long-term Fixes
chunks.content:
### Long-term Fixes
1. **Add startup probe** with generous failure threshold:
   ```yaml
   startupProbe:
     httpGet:
       path: /buying-otherbooking-domain-service/actuator/health
       port: 80
     failureThreshold: 30
     periodSeconds: 5
   ```
2. **Pre-warm DispatcherServlet** - set `spring.mvc.servlet.load-on-startup=1` in config
3. **Increase Istio/VirtualService timeout** for this service if caller timeout is too low
4. **Use `maxSurge: 1, maxUnavailable: 0`** in deployment strategy to ensure old pods stay until new ones are ready

---

chunks.heading: ECU / AllCargo Platform Account - AWS Resources Knowledge Base > 11. INTELLIHUB HIGH AVAILABILITY ASSESSMENT > HA Gaps & Recommendations
chunks.content:
### HA Gaps & Recommendations

| # | Gap | Risk | Recommendation |
|---|-----|------|----------------|
| 1 | **No ASG** | If EC2 instance terminates, no automatic replacement — manual action required | Create ASG (min=1/max=1) per instance for auto-recovery, OR enable **EC2 Auto Recovery** via CloudWatch alarm (`StatusCheckFailed_System`) |
| 2 | **Single-instance services** | `intellihub-prod-genie`, `ecureportsapi-8112`, `doc-disposal`, etc. run on only one server | Move both genie TGs (`intellihub-prod-genie`, `intranet-prod-genie-2`) to point to both instances |
| 3 | **5 stale unused TGs** | Not harmful but causes confusion during incident investigation | Deregister targets and delete unused TGs (`aimlprod-1`, `ecureports`, `ecureports-api`, `intellaiml-prod-4001`, `intellihub-prod-2`) |
| 4 | **Health check interval = 30s** | 60 seconds to detect and remove a failed target (30s interval × 2 unhealthy threshold) | Reduce to 10s interval, keep unhealthy threshold = 2 → 20s failover time |
| 5 | **intranet-prod-db: no Multi-AZ** | Aurora single-instance — DB failure = downtime | Enable Aurora Multi-AZ reader or promote to cluster with failover replica |

chunks.heading: Loop.ai — AWS Cost Breakdown > 6. Operational findings worth acting on > Bounce rate 26.3% — needs attention
chunks.content:
### Bounce rate 26.3% — needs attention

```
8,282 bounces ÷ 31,530 sends = 26.3%
```

AWS's recommended ceiling is **5%**; above 10% risks SES sending pause and
reputation damage. At 26% this is the single biggest risk in the pipeline, and
it also means ~1 in 4 emails is paid for with no delivery.

Fixing this would cut effective cost per *delivered* email by roughly 20%.

### 1. `tariff-selling-rates-ui` Pipeline Fix (`itariff-k8s-repo@develop`, `commit 09ce069`)
- **Problem (Build #133)**: `Install Security Analysis Tools` ran `npm install --save-dev eslint ...`, which mutated `package.json`/`package-lock.json`, installed ESLint v9 (incompatible with `.eslintrc.json` and Node 18), and pruned `style-loader` (causing `npm run build` to fail with missing `style-loader`).
- **Fix**:
  - Changed `--save-dev` to `--no-save` so `package.json` and `package-lock.json` are never mutated.
  - Pinned ESLint v8 (`eslint@^8.57.0`) and included `style-loader css-loader` in the install command so npm never prunes them; exported `ESLINT_USE_FLAT_CONFIG=false`.
  - Added pre-build verification/install of `style-loader` and `css-loader` (`--no-save --legacy-peer-deps`) in `Build Application`.

### Key Architectural Safeguards
1. **Startup Grace Period**: Because EBX deploys large WAR files (~1 GB+), startup takes 3 to 5 minutes. The healer enforces a 180s initial grace period before checking health, avoiding premature restart loops.
2. **HTTP 302 Redirection Handling**: On production, `/ebx/` returns a `302 Moved Temporarily` to `/ebx-ui/`. The health check recognizes 302 as healthy.
3. **Cascade Prevention Cooldown**: A strict 30-minute cooldown prevents rapid restart cycles if the underlying issue is database or storage related.

chunks.heading: 2026-08-17 — ELMA Self-Chat WebSocket Fix & IntelliHub / Intranet Infra (Account 745510282686) > Root Causes (3 layers)
chunks.content:
### Root Causes (3 layers)

**Layer 1 — nginx on Intranet-uat (10.0.132.243)**
- **Root cause (plain terms)**: nginx was stripping the `Upgrade: websocket` header, so every connection got downgraded to HTTP and immediately rejected.
- nginx was running with zero proxy config (default site, no location blocks)
- `/agent/self-chat/ws/` requests hit nginx → `try_files` → `404`
- Fix: Created `/etc/nginx/sites-available/intellihub` with the 4 standard WebSocket proxy directives:
  ```nginx
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
  proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";
  proxy_read_timeout 3600s;
  ```
  These 4 lines are the standard fix for any nginx WebSocket proxy.

**Layer 2 — CloudFront E2FVCC01LF3UUD (elma-dev.allcargoapps.com)**
- CF behavior `/agent/self-chat/ws/*` required trailing wildcard — path `/agent/self-chat/ws/token` didn't always match
- CF behavior allowed only `HEAD, GET` — expanded to all 7 methods
- `/ws` path had no CF behavior — added new behavior
- Fix: Updated path to `/agent/self-chat/ws*`, added `/ws` behavior, both → datascience ALB

**Layer 3 — ALB datascience-144380231 (eu-central-1, account 674017976129)**
- No ALB rule for `/ws` or `/ws/*`
- Fix: Added rule P8 `/ws`, `/ws/*` → `elma-tg:8506`

chunks.content:
### Issue

chunks.heading: 2026-07-24 — DEV EU imdg-prefiler Deep-Link 301/Blank-Page Fix > Root cause
chunks.content:
### Root cause
- `imdg-prefiler` is a single-spa **child** microfrontend (built via `main.single-spa.ts` per `angular.json`, exports `bootstrap`/`mount`/`unmount` lifecycle hooks — does not self-render on script load)
- The Istio `prefiler-ui` VirtualService routes `/imdg-prefiler/*` by path prefix **directly to the `imdg-prefiler-svc` pod**, bypassing the single-spa shell (`microfrontend-main`) entirely
- Shell root (`/`) is where `single-spa` + `single-spa-layout` boot and mount the correct child based on the current URL — a child pod hit directly has no shell, so `main.js` loads but never receives a `mount()` call → blank page
- `imdg-prefiler`'s `.htaccess` had an existing referer-based guard (empty/self referer → 301 to `/dashboard`) specifically to prevent the blank-page case, but it discarded the original path/query, so users landed on the dashboard instead of their intended record
- Git history (`imdg-prefiler` repo) shows this guard was added, removed, and re-added three times via Bitbucket web-UI edits (no PRs) — prior fixes oscillated between "301 to dashboard" (loses destination) and "plain SPA fallback" (blank page), never addressing the actual shell/child routing mismatch
- Root `/` on the shell also has its own `.htaccess` rule (`RedirectMatch ^/$ /login`) that intercepts unauthenticated root requests — relevant when choosing a handoff target

chunks.heading: 2026-07-24 — DEV EU imdg-prefiler Deep-Link 301/Blank-Page Fix > Fix Applied
chunks.content:
### Fix Applied
Two repos, `develop` branch:

**`imdg-prefiler`** (bitbucket.org/allcargoecu/imdg-prefiler, commit `411c520`)
- `.htaccess`: deep-link guard now serves a new `redirector.html` instead of issuing a raw 301
- `redirector.html` (new): client-side JS captures `window.location.pathname + search` and redirects to `https://prefiler-eudev.itopazapp.com/dashboard?spaRedirect=<encoded original path+query>` — uses `/dashboard` (not `/`) to avoid the shell's own `/login` redirect on root
- `Dockerfile`: `ADD redirector.html` alongside `.htaccess` into `htdocs/` root (must sit next to `.htaccess`, not inside the `imdg-prefiler/` subfolder — rewrite substitutions resolve relative to `.htaccess`'s location)

**`microfrontend-main`** (bitbucket.org/allcargoecu/microfrontend-main, commit `6136f1c`)
- `index.html`: before `single-spa`/`single-spa-layout` boot, reads `?spaRedirect=` from the query string and calls `history.replaceState` to restore the real target URL, so `constructRoutes`/`constructApplications` mount the correct child app at the originally requested path

chunks.heading: 2026-06-08 — Cluster Autoscaler Fixes (SIT EU & DEV EU) > Problem Statement
chunks.content:
### Problem Statement

SIT EKS cluster grew from **22 → 33 nodes** while actual workload resource usage remained very low:
- Average CPU utilization: **2–5% per node**
- Average Memory utilization: **18–39% per node**

Cluster Autoscaler was **unable to scale down** nodes due to two default configurations blocking it.

---

chunks.heading: 2026-06-08 — Cluster Autoscaler Fixes (SIT EU & DEV EU) > Blocker 1 — Scale-down utilization threshold too low
chunks.content:
### Blocker 1 — Scale-down utilization threshold too low
CA default `--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.5` (50%)  
Nodes had CPU **requests** above 50% (e.g. 51–97%) even though **actual usage** was only 2–5%.  
CA treats request-based fill, not actual usage → majority of nodes marked **unremovable**.

**CA log evidence:**
```
Node ip-10-100-208-40 unremovable: cpu requested (77.4% of allocatable) is above the scale-down utilization threshold
Node ip-10-100-211-40 unremovable: cpu requested (55.5% of allocatable) is above the scale-down utilization threshold
```

chunks.heading: 2026-06-08 — Cluster Autoscaler Fixes (SIT EU & DEV EU) > Blocker 2 — Local storage eviction disabled by default
chunks.content:
### Blocker 2 — Local storage eviction disabled by default
CA default `--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=true`  
Services using `emptyDir` volumes (ephemeral/temp storage) were preventing node drain.  
All 26 nodes had at least one such pod → **none could be drained**.

**CA log evidence:**
```
Node ip-10-100-215-211 cannot be removed: pod with local storage present: itopaz-profile-service-...
Node ip-10-100-212-208 cannot be removed: pod with local storage present: aes-prefiler-service-...
Node ip-10-100-208-245 cannot be removed: pod with local storage present: tariff-selling-consumer-service-...
```
> **Note:** All affected services are **stateless**. `emptyDir` is ephemeral temp storage — no data loss on pod eviction and rescheduling.

chunks.heading: 2026-06-08 — Cluster Autoscaler Fixes (SIT EU & DEV EU) > Step 2 — Patch: Raise scale-down utilization threshold to 70%
chunks.content:
### Step 2 — Patch: Raise scale-down utilization threshold to 70%
```bash
kubectl patch deployment cluster-autoscaler-aws-cluster-autoscaler \
  -n kube-system \
  --type=json \
  -p='[{"op":"add","path":"REDACTED_SECRET_KEY_PLACEHOLDER_40_CHARS/-","value":"--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.70"}]'
```
**Effect:** CA will now consider a node removable if its total CPU+memory *requests* are below **70%** of allocatable (previously 50%).

chunks.heading: 2026-06-08 — Cluster Autoscaler Fixes (SIT EU & DEV EU) > Step 3 — Patch: Allow eviction of emptyDir pods
chunks.content:
### Step 3 — Patch: Allow eviction of emptyDir pods
```bash
kubectl patch deployment cluster-autoscaler-aws-cluster-autoscaler \
  -n kube-system \
  --type=json \
  -p='[{"op":"add","path":"REDACTED_SECRET_KEY_PLACEHOLDER_40_CHARS/-","value":"--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false"}]'
```
**Effect:** CA will now evict stateless pods using `emptyDir` volumes during node drain. Pods are safely rescheduled onto other nodes with a fresh empty directory.

# EBX Application Auto-Healing & Process Recovery System

Production-grade automated monitoring and auto-healing system for the **TIBCO EBX** application endpoint.

---

chunks.heading: EBX Application Auto-Healing & Process Recovery System > 1. Environment & Target Specifications
chunks.content:
## 1. Environment & Target Specifications

| Parameter | Specification |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Application** | TIBCO EBX (UAT) |
| **Health Check URL** | `https://uat-ecu-tibco.allcargoapps.com/` |
| **AWS Account ID** | `581621506601` (BW-UAT / ECU Allcargo) |
| **AWS SSO Start URL** | `https://ecu-allcargo.awsapps.com/start` |
| **AWS Region** | `us-east-1` |
| **EC2 Instance ID** | `i-0769a14e8d55cb971` |

chunks.heading: EBX Application Auto-Healing & Process Recovery System > 2. Problem Statement & Design Objectives > The Problem
chunks.content:
### The Problem
Previously, intermittent HTTP 404 or 500 errors caused immediate application restarts or full server reboots. This resulted in:
1. False-alarm restart loops during transient network glitches or high-load spikes.
2. Extended downtime as EBX requires 2 to 5 minutes to initialize its database connections and application contexts.
3. Unnecessary rebooting of the underlying EC2 instance, killing all other co-located processes.

chunks.heading: EBX Application Auto-Healing & Process Recovery System > 2. Problem Statement & Design Objectives > Design Objectives
chunks.content:
### Design Objectives
- **Consecutive Failure Threshold**: Require **3 consecutive failed health checks** before taking any recovery action. Single errors do not trigger restarts.
- **Short-Interval Retries**: When an unhealthy status is detected, retry after **30 seconds** (instead of the normal 60 seconds).
- **Process Status Validation**: Verify whether the EBX process is running, crashed, or unresponsive before issuing a restart.
- **Process-Only Restart**: Restart only the EBX Tomcat service/process via `systemctl` or native shutdown/startup scripts. **Zero server reboots**.
- **Post-Restart Startup Verification**: Wait for EBX startup grace period (90s) and actively poll for **HTTP 200** for up to 300 seconds.
- **Restart Cooldown (Anti-Loop Protection)**: Enforce a **30-minute cooldown** period. If the application continues failing after a restart, do **not** restart repeatedly.
- **Alerting & Logging**: Dispatches structured alerts via AWS SNS, Microsoft Teams, Slack, and local audit logs.

---

EBX Application Auto-Healing & Process Recovery System > 6. Deployment Guide > Option A: Local Installation directly on EC2 (`i-0769a14e8d55cb971`)
chunks.content:
### Option A: Local Installation directly on EC2 (`i-0769a14e8d55cb971`)

1. Copy the `ebx-auto-healing` directory to the target server `10.233.30.118`:
   ```bash
   scp -i /home/ec2-REDACTED_SECRET_KEY_PLACEHOLDER_40_CHARSdm/dev/EC2-EBX-Server-Key.pem -r \
       /home/ec2-user/rahul/scripts/ebx-auto-healing ec2-user@10.233.30.118:/tmp/
   ```

2. SSH to the instance and execute the installer:
   ```bash
   ssh -i /home/ec2-REDACTED_SECRET_KEY_PLACEHOLDER_40_CHARSdm/dev/EC2-EBX-Server-Key.pem ec2-user@10.233.30.118
   cd /tmp/ebx-auto-healing
   sudo bash install.sh
   ```

3. Enable and start the systemd daemon:
   ```bash
   sudo systemctl enable ebx-auto-heal
   sudo systemctl start ebx-auto-heal
   ```

4. Verify service status and logs:
   ```bash
   sudo systemctl status ebx-auto-heal
   sudo tail -f /var/log/ebx-auto-heal.log
   ```
